why: Subclass ladder is the AI recommendation at 88.5/100, first for both judges (user lens 91, maintainer lens 86). It is the most literal reading of 'Model as the base object': each rung is a typed frozen dataclass whose fields are its parameters and whose MRO is its fallback, and it fits, predicts on arrays, scores held-out data and exports MuJoCo attributes itself. Its price is upkeep: until the classes become the source, every rung is written twice (class + Rung record), a new rung needs a class, a record, the rung folder and a seeds() override (fr5 = 2 from both judges), and a Rung added without a class silently drops out of its ladder. Closest alternative: Estimators that climb at 83.0, where one call, servo.climb(datasheet, fit, test), answers 'what now' as an additive layer over v1.
hinge: The lead rests on fr1 (the Model you hold) against fr4/fr5 (migration, cost of a new rung). Moving about 10 points from fr1 to fr4 lets Records in a Family tie Estimators that climb for first (its Family subclasses today's Ladder; sim2real's parity test passed 56 with Families in place of Ladders). Reading 'what now' as 'tell me which rig motion to run next' lifts Type kit level with Estimators that climb. Neither flip overtakes Subclass ladder unless migration or rung cost is weighted up. The contested assumption is judging it on its end state (the class tree replaces ladder.py's records, a ruler edit) rather than on the interim duplicate.
